newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: BADMINTON-DEFENDING CHAMPION GOES OUT IN MALAYSIA.
newsitem.headline: BADMINTON-DEFENDING CHAMPION GOES OUT IN MALAYSIA.

text.p: Defending champion Ong Ewe Hock of Malaysia crashed out of the Malaysian Open badminton championships on Friday after a 10-15 15-6 15-11 quarter-final defeat by Indonesian Santoso Budi.

On a poor day for the big names, compatriot and three-times champion Rashid Sidek also went out when he was beaten 15-5 15-6 by Indonesia's Hermawan Susanto at the Likas arena in Malaysia's eastern Sabah state.
Tournament top seed Joko Suprianto of Indonesia, however, lived up to his billing when he beat Lou Yigang of China 15-10, 11-15, 18-14 in a gruelling 105-minute battle to reach the semifinals.
Denmark's Peter Gate Christiansen, the sole European survivor in the tournament, stopped Alan Budi Kusuma of Indonesia, 18-17, 15-11 in the other quarter-final.
